models_evaluated: RaySearch RayStation v12a automatic planning (U-Net dose prediction plus dose mimicking), baseline and two tuned iterations

links.outcome: Local historical plan quality of automated plans versus clinical plans, and effect of tuning
links.effect: Baseline model had inferior rectum sparing (mean rectum V40Gy 0.04 higher); after two tuning iterations, differences were small (mean difference -0.01 rectum V40Gy, -0.03 PTV48 D98%).
links.quote: The Bland–Altman plots, supplementary Material S4, showed little difference between the original and automated plans for the third iteration.

links.outcome: Whether tuning the model on selected local cases improved plan quality
links.effect: Two further model iterations tuned on locally selected cases produced comparable rectum sparing (0.02 mean difference in rectum V50Gy) while keeping much of the improved consistency.
links.quote: Further iterations of the model resulted in comparable rectum sparing, a 0.02 mean difference in rectum V50 Gy, was achieved whilst maintaining much of the improved consistency.

links.outcome: Feasibility of control-chart (Wald sequential test) monitoring of plan quality on validation cases
links.effect: Monitoring null hypothesis rejected quickly: after 10, 13 and 12 cases for the tested metrics; more than the 18 validation cases were needed in many cases to accept or reject hypotheses.
links.quote: This was reflected in the rapid rejection of H1; after 10 cases for PTV60 Gy D 98 % , 13 cases for PTV60 Gy D 98 % and 12 cases for the MCS.

links.outcome: Ability of CUSUM-based monitoring to detect deviations in plan quality metrics
links.effect: Wald sequential mean and variance tests reached decisions in tens of cases (delta=0.5) using 18 validation cases; validated as a post-deployment monitoring method.
links.quote: Two process control metrics have been demonstrated to monitor the introduction of AI planning into routine practice to ensure that the real-world performance was consistent with that projected.

links.outcome: Plan quality of automated plans adjusted for anatomy and across risk groups
links.effect: High-risk cases had better coverage so tuning selection was biased toward them; intermediate-risk cases fell below D99% threshold in iteration two, prompting a third iteration with intermediate-risk cases.
links.quote: High risk cases generally had better coverage and so the quantile regression based selection was biased towards them.

models_evaluated: Raystation v12a automatic planning baseline model
Raystation v12a automatic planning model iteration 2
Raystation v12a automatic planning model iteration 3

links.effect: Initial automated plans had rectum V40Gy 0.04 (σ = 0.04) greater than original plans.
links.quote: The mean rectum V 40 G y was 0.04 ( σ = 0 . 04 ) greater for the automated plans in the initial evaluation ( Fig. 1(a) ).

links.effect: Final iteration mean difference −0.03 for PTV48 Gy D98% and −0.01 for rectum V40Gy.
links.quote: PTV coverage and rectum sparing was almost identical between the two groups, with a mean difference −0.03 for PTV48 Gy D 98 % coverage and −0.01 for rectum V 40 G y .

links.effect: After further iterations, rectum V50 Gy mean difference was 0.02 while consistency was maintained.
links.quote: Further iterations of the model resulted in comparable rectum sparing, a 0.02 mean difference in rectum V50 Gy, was achieved whilst maintaining much of the improved consistency.

links.effect: Iteration 2 caused some PTV48 Gy D98% results below mandatory D99% threshold; iteration 3 was produced.
links.quote: In some cases the PTV 48 Gy D 98 % fell below the mandatory D99% threshold and so iteration three of the model was produced.

links.effect: MCS showed automated plans more complex; MCS intercept 0.24 vs 0.29 and σ 0.04 vs 0.06.
links.quote: Metrics such as the MCS revealed a difference in the range of complexities, demonstrating the importance of considering more than only dose-volume metrics.

links.effect: More than 18 validation cases were required in many cases; selected metrics rejected H1 after 10, 13, and 12 cases.
links.quote: More than the 18 validation cases were required in many cases to accept or reject the null hypothesis in the monitoring validation.

links.outcome: rectum sparing and plan quality consistency
links.effect: Model tuning achieved comparable rectum sparing (0.02 mean difference in rectum V50 Gy) while maintaining improved plan consistency.
links.quote: Further iterations of the model resulted in comparable rectum sparing, a 0.02 mean difference in rectum V50 Gy, was achieved whilst maintaining much of the improved consistency.
